---
title: "Thicket-specific intensity refinement"
---

## Summary

Biome-specific ecosystem condition information is being tested as an additional source of land use intensity for BII segments classified as untransformed within the Thicket biome.

In solid Thicket, mapped ecological condition is strongly associated with rangeland use intensity, particularly browsing by domestic livestock. The condition probabilities are therefore converted to a continuous intensity score for BII use.

## Input data

-   National BII segment raster.
-   National BII land use reclassification.
-   National protected area layer.
-   Thicket ecosystem functional group boundaries:

``` text
projects/thicket-ecological-condition/assets/ThicketEFGs
```

-   Thicket ecosystem condition probability surfaces:

``` text
projects/thicket-ecological-condition/assets/RF_prob_surfaces_solid_thicket_2025
```

The probability raster contains:

``` text
p_intact
p_moderate
p_severe
```

## Data preparation

The national segment workflow is clipped to the mapped Thicket biome extent.

The pixel-level Thicket intensity score is calculated as:

$$
I = 0.5p_{moderate} + p_{severe}
$$

This assigns the following class endpoints:

| Condition | Intensity contribution |
|-----------|-----------------------:|
| Intact    |                      0 |
| Moderate  |                    0.5 |
| Severe    |                      1 |

Only valid, unmasked probability pixels are used. Pixels masked in the probability raster were excluded from the condition model because they were already transformed, water or otherwise outside the modelled natural extent.

## Analysis

Valid pixel-level scores are averaged within each segment. The Thicket-derived score is used only to refine the intensity of segments assigned to the Untransformed BII land use class. The dominant BII land use allocation remains unchanged. Transformed classes retain their national BII intensity rules.

Two protected area treatments were initially compared:

1.  apply the Thicket intensity score to untransformed and protected segments; and

2.  retain protected areas at an intensity of 0.

## Output

The Thicket test output follows the national two-band structure:

``` text
bii_land_use
bii_land_use_intensity
```

The workflow will later be extended as equivalent biome-specific intensity datasets become available.
